draft.title: Death and the afterlife in Egypt
card: Ancient Egyptians believed that life continued after death. They thought the soul could live on only if the body was kept safe.
Wealthy Egyptians had their bodies mummified. This meant the body was dried and wrapped so that it would not rot.
The dead were buried with goods such as food, furniture and jewellery. People believed these things would be needed in the afterlife.
Early pharaohs were buried in pyramids. Later, tombs were hidden in rock to protect the body and the goods from robbers.
draft.remember: Egyptians kept the body and buried goods with it, because they thought the soul needed both to live on.

a.q: Why did wealthy Egyptians have their bodies mummified?
opts: They believed the soul needed the body to be kept safe
They believed a rotting body would harm the living
They wanted the body to be easy to move to a pyramid
They wanted to show the pharaoh how rich the family was
a.why: Egyptians believed the soul needed the body to be kept safe, so mummifying stopped it rotting. Showing off wealth may have been a side effect, but it was not the belief behind mummification.
a.clue: Think about what the soul was believed to need.

b.q: Archaeologists open an Egyptian tomb and find a mummy with jars of food, a wooden bed and jewellery. What do these goods best show?
opts: People believed the dead would need them in the afterlife
People believed the goods would stop the body from rotting
People believed the goods would keep tomb robbers away
People believed the goods were payment to the priests
b.why: Food, a bed and jewellery were things a person used in life. Egyptians buried them so the dead could use them in the afterlife. The goods did not stop rot, which is why the body was mummified.
b.clue: Ask what a person would want after death.

a.best: They believed the soul needed the body to be kept safe

b.best: People believed the dead would need them in the afterlife
